[Resource from qmd at qmd://github-docs/content/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/configuring-pull-request-merges/about-merge-methods-on-github.md] 1: ---
2: title: About merge methods on GitHub
3: intro: 'You can allow contributors with push access to your repository to merge their pull requests with different merge options or enforce a specific merge method for all of your repository''s pull requests.'
4: redirect_from:
5:   - /articles/about-merge-methods-on-github
6:   - /github/administering-a-repository/about-merge-methods-on-github
7:   - /github/administering-a-repository/configuring-pull-request-merges/about-merge-methods-on-github
8: versions:
9:   fpt: '*'
10:   ghes: '*'
11:   ghec: '*'
12: shortTitle: About merge methods
13: category:
14:   - Configure merges and pull requests
15: ---
16: {% data reusables.pull_requests.configure_pull_request_merges_intro %} You can enforce one type of merge method, such as commit squashing or rebasing, by only enabling the desired method for your repository.
17: 
18: > [!NOTE]
19: > When using the merge queue, you no longer get to choose the merge method, as this is controlled by the queue. {% data reusables.pull_requests.merge-queue-references %}
20: {% ifversion repo-rules-merge-type -%}
21: >
22: > Merge methods set on the repository that conflict with the merge method rule will prevent merging. For example if you do not allow rebase merging for the repository, and the merge rule only allows rebase on a branch, that merge will not be possible. For more information, see [AUTOTITLE](/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-rulesets/available-rules-for-rulesets#require-a-pull-request-before-merging).
23: {%- endif %}
24: 
25: {% data reusables.pull_requests.default_merge_option %}
26: 
27: The default merge method creates a merge commit. You can prevent anyone from pushing merge commits to a protected branch by enforcing a linear commit history. For more information, see [AUTOTITLE](/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-protected-branches/about-protected-branches#require-linear-history).
28: 
29: ## Squashing your merge commits
30: 
31: {% data reusables.pull_requests.squash_and_merge_summary %}
32: 
33: Before enabling squashing commits, consider these disadvantages:
34: * You lose information about when specific changes were originally made and who authored the squashed commits.
35: * If you continue working on the head branch of a pull request after squashing and merging, and then create a new pull request between the same branches, commits that you previously squashed and merged will be listed in the new pull request. You may also have conflicts that you have to repeatedly resolve in each successive pull request. For more information, see [AUTOTITLE](/pull-requests/reference/pull-request-merges#squashing-and-merging-a-long-running-branch).
36: * Some Git commands that use the "SHA" or "hash" ID may be harder to use since the SHA ID for the original commits is lost. For example, using [`git rerere`](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-rerere) may not be as effective.
37: 
38: For more information, see [AUTOTITLE](/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/configuring-pull-request-merges/configuring-commit-squashing-for-pull-requests).
39: 
40: ## Rebasing and merging your commits

content.text:
Yes — GitHub supports this via **repository rulesets**, not classic branch protection.

**Docs:** `repositories/…/managing-rulesets/available-rules-for-rulesets.md`, section **"Require a pull request before merging"** (line 131-132):

> "Optionally, you can require a merge type of merge, squash, or rebase. This means the targeted branches may only be merged based on the allowed type."

So: create a ruleset targeting `production`, enable **Require a pull request before merging**, and set the allowed merge method to **Merge commit** only. This is enforced only for the targeted branch, unlike the repo-wide "Allow squash merging" toggle. Note (from `configuring-pull-request-merges/about-merge-methods-on-github.md`): your repo must still have that merge method enabled at the repo level, or the merge will be blocked.
